title: The heartbeat

data.source: PhysioNet, RR interval time series from healthy subjects (Irurzun et al. 2021), records 000, 002, 003, 005

prediction: With q chosen on the first half of each day, the seed rule predicts the next beat interval on the second half with lower RMSE than both persistence and an AR(8) model, in at least 3 of 4 people.
baseline: Persistence, the running mean of the last 300 beats, and an AR(8) model fitted on the first half.
why: The seed rule beat "repeat the last beat" in three of four people, but it lost to the ordinary AR(8) model in three of four. A short running average helps a little; the standard model, which can follow the rhythm of breathing, helps more.
